Package neqsim.process.measurementdevice

Class DifferentialPressureFlowMeter

java.lang.Object
neqsim.util.NamedBaseClass
neqsim.process.measurementdevice.MeasurementDeviceBaseClass
neqsim.process.measurementdevice.StreamMeasurementDeviceBaseClass
neqsim.process.measurementdevice.DifferentialPressureFlowMeter
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, TransientStateParticipant<DifferentialPressureFlowMeter.DifferentialPressureFlowMeterState>, MeasurementDeviceInterface, ProcessElementInterface, NamedInterface
Direct Known Subclasses:
ConeFlowMeter, NozzleFlowMeter, OrificeFlowMeter, VenturiFlowMeter, WedgeFlowMeter
public abstract class DifferentialPressureFlowMeter extends StreamMeasurementDeviceBaseClass implements TransientStateParticipant<DifferentialPressureFlowMeter.DifferentialPressureFlowMeterState>
Shared physics for differential-pressure primary devices following ISO 5167-1 (general principles) and its device-specific parts: ISO 5167-2 (orifice plates), ISO 5167-3 (nozzles), ISO 5167-4 (classical Venturi tubes), ISO 5167-5 (cone meters) and ISO 5167-6 (wedge meters).

Every part expands the same ISO 5167-1 general equation 

 qm = C / sqrt(1 - beta ^ 4) * epsilon * (pi / 4) * d ^ 2 * sqrt(2 * dP * rho1)

with Re,D = 4 qm / (pi mu1 D) and Re,d = Re,D / beta. The parts differ only in how the discharge coefficient C and the expansibility factor epsilon are computed from the geometry, the Reynolds number and the isentropic exponent; that is exactly the split between calcDischargeCoefficient(double, double) and getExpansibilityModel() that each concrete device implements.

The geometry is stored as an upstream pipe internal diameter D and a throat diameter d, with the diameter ratio beta = d / D always recomputed on demand from the two. Devices with no physical throat bore (the ISO 5167-5 cone meter and the ISO 5167-6 wedge meter) derive an equivalent d = D beta from their own geometry (cone diameter, wedge gap height) and store that instead, so this base class only ever needs the one (D, d) representation.

The differential pressure is either set explicitly with setDifferentialPressure(double, String) or read from a linked DifferentialPressureTransmitter, which takes precedence when present. The upstream gas density, the isentropic exponent and the dynamic viscosity are all read from the connected stream's gas phase by default (falling back to the mixture when no gas phase is present), and can each be overridden with a sampling-derived value.

    • calcDischargeCoefficient

      protected abstract double calcDischargeCoefficient(double beta, double reynoldsD)
      Calculates the discharge coefficient C for the given diameter ratio and pipe Reynolds number. Devices whose coefficient does not depend on the Reynolds number (classical Venturi tubes, cone and wedge meters) simply ignore the second argument.
      Parameters:
      beta - diameter ratio d/D [-]
      reynoldsD - pipe Reynolds number Re,D [-]; an initial estimate of 1.0e6 is used for the first iteration
      Returns:
      discharge coefficient C [-]

    • setThroatDiameter

      public void setThroatDiameter(double throatDiameter, String unit)
      Sets the throat diameter d directly. Devices with a physical throat bore (orifice, nozzle, classical Venturi) normally use setGeometry(double, double, String) instead; devices with no physical throat (cone, wedge) derive this value from their own geometry, passing Double.NaN to mark the geometry as unset/invalid (see e.g. WedgeFlowMeter.setWedgeRatio(double)) rather than a positive throat diameter.
      Parameters:
      throatDiameter - throat diameter, normally positive; Double.NaN marks unset/invalid geometry
      unit - length unit, one of "m", "cm", "mm" or "in"

    • getMassFlowRatePerSecond

      protected double getMassFlowRatePerSecond()
      Solves the dry-gas ISO 5167-1 general equation, iterating on the pipe Reynolds number when calcDischargeCoefficient(double, double) depends on it. Devices with a Reynolds-number-independent discharge coefficient converge on the first pass. Never throws.
      Returns:
      mass flow rate [kg/sec], 0.0 when the differential pressure is not positive and NaN when the inputs are not physically valid

    • getVolumeFlowRate

      public double getVolumeFlowRate(String unit)
      Returns the actual (flowing-condition) volume flow rate. Standard-volume units (e.g. "Sm3/hr") are delegated to getStandardVolumeFlowRate(String) since the flowing gas density used here would otherwise be paired with a standard-volume unit, which is dimensionally inconsistent.
      Parameters:

      Returns:
      actual (or standard, when a standard-volume unit is requested) volume flow rate in the requested unit

    • getStandardVolumeFlowRate

      public double getStandardVolumeFlowRate(String unit)
      Returns the standard-condition volume flow rate, using the standard density (15 degC, 1 atm) of the stream fluid. The gas-phase molar mass is used when a gas phase is present (falling back to the mixture molar mass otherwise), so a wet-gas stream's liquid content does not bias the reported gas standard volume flow.
      Parameters:
      unit - standard volume flow unit, one of "Sm3/sec", "Sm3/hr", "Sm3/day", "kSm3/hr" or "MSm3/day"
      Returns:
      standard volume flow rate in the requested unit
